h:
You weren’t raised by apostles. You were groomed by Rome.

That’s why you:

  • flinch at Torah,
  • confuse grace with lawlessness,
  • fear judgment more than sin,
  • and treat the King’s constitution like it’s expired.

Let’s break the spell.

1. You Were Taught to Fear the Father and Cling to the Son

The Roman church painted Yah as the angry Old Testament God and Jesus as the nice, New Testament upgrade.

But Yahusha said:

“I and the Father are one.”

If your gospel divides the nature of the God you claim to follow, you weren’t raised in the Kingdom. You were raised in Rome, where the Son is used to silence the Father.

2. You Were Trained to Feel Saved, Not Bear Fruit

You were told:

“Just believe and receive.”

No discipleship. No discipline. Just altar calls and emotional highs.

But Yahusha said:

“By their fruits you will know them.”

Rome gave you therapy. The Kingdom gives you transformation.

Sons don’t just claim salvation. They manifest evidence.

3. You Call Any Standard “Legalism”

You were trained to equate structure with slavery. Any demand for obedience? Legalism. Any talk of Torah? Religion.

But the Kingdom is not chaos. It is law, rank, and order.

If correction offends you more than sin, Rome still lives in your bloodstream.

4. You Think Heaven Is the Goal

Rome taught you that salvation is an escape plan. Get saved, stay nice, and go to Heaven when you die.

But the Kingdom teaches:

“The meek shall inherit the Earth.”

Yahusha didn’t say pray to escape. He said pray:

“Thy Kingdom come, Thy will be done on Earth.”

Sons don’t run. They rule.

5. You Think Freedom Means No Rules

Rome made you allergic to commandments.

They told you that grace means doing what you feel.

But in the Kingdom:

  • Grace is the power to obey.
  • Freedom is submission to divine structure.
  • Liberty is walking in Spirit-led alignment with Torah.

If your version of freedom hates order, it’s rebellion, not righteousness.

You were raised under Rome if:

  • you worship a Son who overthrows His Father,
  • you think love cancels law,
  • and you believe faith means no fruit.

But the remnant is waking up. The ones trained by the King Himself. The ones who know the government is on His shoulders, and that includes His law.

Rome trained you to be a religious slave.
The Kingdom trains you to be a righteous ruler.
